feed.title: NPR Topics: Business
feed.subtitle: Find the latest business news with reports on Wall Street, interest rates, banking, companies, and U.S. and world financial markets. Subscribe to the Business Story of the Day podcast.

entry.title: How the beverage aisle got so wild
entry.summary: Planet Money traced many new beverage flavors to one laboratory that serves dozens of companies to see how new flavors are created and why we're seeing such an explosion of options right now.

entry.title: Despite the controversy, data centers could be attractive to struggling rural towns
entry.summary: There's lots of debate over data centers and where they should be located. In a struggling rural town data center development can look a lot more attractive.

entry.title: How the oil industry is preparing for Hurricane Isaias
entry.summary: Hurricane Isaias is this season's first Atlantic hurricane, and is on a path to hit the northern Gulf Coast. How is the oil industry preparing?

entry.title: Why American investors love European defense startups
entry.summary: As European defense spending takes off, just about half of the funding in Europe's defense tech industry is coming from American investors this year. One reason why: European investment firms have restrictions on how they can invest.

entry.title: OpenAI caught Russians and Iranians using ChatGPT for influence campaigns
entry.summary: The company says Russian operatives used its AI chatbot to update their bosses, shedding light on influence campaigns previously not attributed to Russia.

entry.title: As crypto and prediction markets expand, their regulator shrinks
entry.summary: Even as the agency is tasked with drawing up new rules for crypto and prediction markets, its staffing and enforcement actions have dropped precipitously during the second Trump administration.

entry.title: Why Trump just loosened the rules on 'dyed diesel' — normally a farm fuel
entry.summary: Trump is temporarily allowing this fuel to be used on highways, although it's typically just for off-road farm and construction vehicles. Could that lower the price of diesel?

entry.title: Who will win the 2026 Nobel Prize in economics?
entry.summary: A thinly traded prediction market offers a starting point. We explore potential winners and the big ideas that could earn them economics' biggest prize.

entry.title: Here's the latest sticker shock: Borrowing for a mortgage -- or a car
entry.summary: It's not just mortgages being at their highest level in almost three years — but the cost of loans for cars and higher education are among the borrowing costs affected, too.

entry.title: Jennifer Welch isn't holding back on Trump, Democrats or political division
entry.summary: The podcaster talks to Leila Fadel about her new book, her evolving politics and what it means to build a future with people whose views she strongly opposes.
